Read the diff, both touched files, the sibling OPF test file, and `cmd/entire/cli/testutil`. Four reuse findings, ranked.

## 1. `remoteCommitMessage` re-implements `testutil.RunGit` — and the shell-out isn't needed at all

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/refs_push_test.go:396-404` (new helper)

The 9-line helper hand-rolls `exec.CommandContext` + `testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()` + `CombinedOutput` + `require.NoError`. That is exactly `testutil.RunGit`:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/testutil/testutil.go:181
func RunGit(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) string
```

Its body (`gitenv.Run`, `cmd/entire/cli/testutil/gitenv/gitenv.go:153-163`) sets `cmd.Dir`, `cmd.Env = Isolated()`, runs `CombinedOutput`, and `t.Fatalf`s on error — byte-for-byte the same behaviour. The whole helper collapses to one line:

```go
return testutil.RunGit(t, bareDir, "log", "-1", "--format=%B", hash)
```

`RunGit` is already imported and used twice in this same file (lines 56, 135).

Better still: drop the shell-out. Every other OPF-trailer assertion in the package reads the commit through go-git — `repo.CommitObject(h)` then `trailers.HasOPFApplied(commit.Message)` (`manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:946-948`) — and opening the bare remote with `git.PlainOpen(bareDir)` and calling `bareRepo.Reference(...)` is the established in-package pattern (`push_common_test.go:179-182`). Doing that also removes the second `ls-remote` round trip the new test makes via `remoteRefHash` just to get a hash to feed back to `git log`.

## 2. The two new tests hand-roll a setup `setupGitRefsOPFRepo` already provides

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/refs_push_test.go:333-342` and `367-376`

Both tests repeat a 5-statement preamble: `setupRepoWithCheckpointRefs` → `t.Chdir` → `paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()` → `git.PlainOpen` → `enqueueRefs`. The OPF half of the package already has a single-call equivalent:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:826
func setupGitRefsOPFRepo(t *testing.T, cpIDs ...string) (bareDir string, repo *git.Repository, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName)
```

It does init+commit, the git-refs backend setting, a bare origin, the `origin` remote, `t.Chdir`, `paths.ClearWorktreeRootCache()` **plus the `t.Cleanup` the new tests omit** (line 846), and queues every ref by doing a real backend write. It is what `TestRewriteQueuedCheckpointRefsWithOPF_*` and `TestPrePushCheckpointRefs_OPF*` (lines 932, 959, 973) all use. `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo, bareDir)` takes the target as a plain string, so the returned `bareDir` drops straight in.

Concrete cost beyond the ~10 duplicated lines: `setupRepoWithCheckpointRefs` points the refs at a plain `README.md` commit, so the new "OPF applied" test can only assert the trailer. `setupGitRefsOPFRepo` writes sessions containing the `PERSONABC` sentinel the fake redacts, which is how the sibling test also asserts the content was actually scrubbed (`require.NotContains(treeContents(...), "PERSONABC")`, line 949).

The one thing it doesn't return is the `*checkpoint.PushQueue` handle. That is already solved too:

```go
// cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:923
func queuedRefs(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository) []plumbing.ReferenceName
```

Non-destructive (`Peek`), and it is what `TestPrePushCheckpointRefs_OPFDisabledFlushesUnchanged:1004` uses for the identical "pushed refs leave the queue" assertion — replacing the `queue.Drain()` pair in both new tests.

## 3. The inline `ls-remote` + `NotContains` block is the third verbatim copy in the package

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/refs_push_test.go:387-393`

Identical to `refs_push_test.go:277-283` (same file, 110 lines up, differing only in the `lsErr` variable name and the assert message), and a near-copy of `manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:987-991`. It sits below the `dupl` threshold, so nothing will flag it.

There is no existing named "assert refs absent from remote" helper — I checked. But `testutil.RunGit` (`testutil.go:181`, signature above) already replaces four of the five lines:

```go
out := testutil.RunGit(t, bareDir, "ls-remote", bareDir)
for _, ref := range refs {
    assert.NotContains(t, out, ref.String(), "withheld push must not reach the remote")
}
```

The right move is to extract one `assertRefsAbsentFromRemote(t, bareDir, refs...)` next to the existing `remoteRefHash`/`remoteRefFiles` helpers (`refs_push_test.go:305-325`) and point all three call sites at it.

## 4. Production side: the withheld-push sentence now exists twice in one file

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:452-454` (new)

```go
return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("OPF did not run, so checkpoint refs stay queued: %w", opfErr)
```

duplicates the user-facing wording already in `warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld`, 165 lines earlier in the same file:

```go
// manual_commit_push.go:281-282
"[entire] OPF did not run, so checkpoint refs were not pushed and stay queued for your next push: %v\n"
```

Same condition, two hand-maintained phrasings of the same sentence — the exact drift the refactor was meant to avoid on the decision side. I found no reusable sentinel or constructor: `warnOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld` prints and returns nothing, and there is no `ErrOPFCheckpointRefsWithheld`. So this needs a small new shared piece (a message const, or an `opfCheckpointRefsWithheldErr(err) error` that the warn function formats), not a call to something existing. Lowest-value finding of the four; flagging it because the diff is what created the second copy.

## Correctly reused, no finding

The new tests reuse `configureFakeOPF` / `fakeOPFForRewrite` / `fakeRuntimeAlwaysFails` / `batchCallCount` (`manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:34-107`) and `enqueueRefs` (`refs_push_test.go:199`) rather than building new fakes — that part is clean. No duplication found on the `opfGateForCheckpointRefs` refactor itself.
